newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australian Broadcasting Corp Morning Update.
newsitem.headline: Australian Broadcasting Corp Morning Update.

text.p: MONKEY TRIAL MARK II OPENS IN SYDNEY
For the second time this century evolutionists and creationists will go to court, but in Monkey Trial Mark II, which opens in Sydney today, it's the evolutionists taking on the creationists.
The trial has attracted international attention and has been dubbed Monkey Trial Mark II in honour of the 1925 trial of an American science teacher for teaching Darwin's theory of evolution.
Ian Plimer, Professor of Geology and Head of the School of Earth Sciences at Melbourne University is accusing Alan Roberts, a Doctor of Christian Education, of breaching the Trade Practises Act.

Professor Plimer claims the Christian Doctor is engaging in misleading and deceptive conduct by arguing in books, videos, brochures and lectures that the earth is just 6000 years old, that a great flood 4000 years ago triggered global mass extinctions and that all species alive today emerged safe and sound from Noah's Ark.
ANOTHER FOOD RECALL IN VICTORIA
There's another food recall in Victoria...this time it's cheese from a Thomastown factory.
The recall comes as authorities plan a national meeting on food standards today, where uniform regulations will be considered in the wake of food poisoning outbreaks in several states.
In the latest incident in Victoria, Floridia Cheese says its 500 gram packs of Provollette Salamini cheese may have been contaminated.
The company says the contamination might affect young people, old people or pregnant women.
FOUNDATION SET UP TO BANKROLL SERIAL KILLER HUNT
The family of murdered Perth woman Ciara Glennon have asked people who intend sending flowers to instead donate to a fund set up to help catch her killer.
A family friend has told the AB- money should be donated to the Secure Community Foundation, which is providing funds to help the police track down the killer.
Ms Glennon's murder has been linked to the death of another young woman, and the disappearance of a third, sparking fears that a serial killer may be responsible.
Ciara Glennon's body was found in bush north of Perth four days ago, and since then her family has been inundated with calls of sympathy and bouquets of flowers.
The Secure Community Foundation has been set up by Ms Glennon's friends and law firm colleagues, and is already committed to a $250,000 advertising campaign which began last night.
TELSTRA LEGAL ACTIONS CONCERN COMPETITORS
Telecommunications service providers are concerned Telstra is attempting to bully competitors to keep control of Australia's telecommunications market prior to further deregulation.

The Service Providers' Action Network says it's seeking an urgent meeting with the Communications Minister to press for an inquiry into Telstra's billing procedures, and its legal action against competitors.
Executive director, Alan Brand, says Telstra is taking legal action against two of its largest service provider competitors.
He says billing procedures are at the root of disputes between service providers and the carrier.
EUTHANASIA SOCIETY TARGETS PRE-SELECTION PROCESS
The Northern Territory's voluntary euthanasia society has called for supporters in political parties to warn their party branches euthanasia will be a key election issue.
The Society's Lynda Cracknell says a letter has been sent out to encourage pre-selection of candidates supporting voluntary euthanasia.
The move follows the overriding of the Territory's right to die law by the Andrews bill in the Federal Parliament. Carers' group says Budget help needed to stop poverty trap

CARERS' GROUP SAYS BUDGET HELP NEEDED TO STOP POVERTY TRAP The Carers' Association of Australia is urging the Federal Government to alleviate the financial stress suffered by family carers in next month's Budget.
Senior researcher, David Fisher, says carers are among the poorest people in Australia.

The association is calling on the Government to increase the rate of domicilairy nursing care benefit, extend the carer pension to children under the age of 16, introduce an indexed carer payment or wage within the next five years and abolish sales tax on medical aids.
Mr Fisher says without a major policy overhaul, many of Australia's one-and-a-half million carers will be trapped in poverty.
QLD GOVT SAYS WELFARE FUND LIABILITY NEEDS COURT DECISION
Queensland's Community Care Minister says he'll abide by a Federal Court decision on how much money is owed to Aborigines through the state's welfare fund.
Kev Lingard says there has always been concern about the welfare fund but the amount owed can only be determined by a court.
ATSIC Deputy-Chairman, Ray Robinson, has said Aborigines are preparing to take the state to court in a 300-million dollar class action over unpaid wages held in the Indigenous Welfare Fund.
This follows a successful campaign by six Palm Island elders to recover wages owed since the Bjelke-Petersen era.
PACIFIC REGION AIR FORCES MEET IN DARWIN
Disaster relief co-operation and flying safety will be the focus of a meeting of Pacific area air force officers beginning in Darwin today.
Representatives from the United States, Japanese, Indonesian, Thai, and Bangladeshi air forces will take part in the conference.
The Pacific Area Air Force director of Operations conferences are held every six months, with the last meeting hosted in Alaska.
A Defence Force spokesperson says the conference will include presentations from representatives of Northern Command, and the Northern Territory Government.
The visitors are due to leave on Friday morning after visits to Tindall Air Force base near Katherine, and the Delamere bombing range.

NSW WANTS RESIDENTIAL AGED CARE PROPOSAL BACKED WITH FUNDING Community Services Minister Ron Dyer says the state government won't accept a federal proposal to transfer responsibility for residential aged care to the states without extra funds.
Mr Dyer says New South Wales has no qualms about accepting responsibility for caring for old people, under a proposal flagged by the Federal Government last year.
But he says it can't fulfil the responsibility without guarantees of ongoing funding.
The Minister says the Federal Government must give the states extra resources if it's serious about reforming the aged care system.
He'll address a rally in Sydney later today by the New South Wales Aged Care Alliance.
AID ORGANISATION SAYS LAND RELATED TO INDIGENOUS HEALTH
Aid organisation PLAN International has joined the Australian Medical Association in calling for the resolution of land ownership issues as a step towards improving indigenous health.
Executive director Tricia Caswell says PLAN has found the connection between land and health is very probable.

Ms Caswell says land is very much connected to the future health, wealth and well-being of indigenous communities and people who have been uprooted from their land are particularly vulnerable to poor health.
ACF CALLS ON FEDERAL GOVT TO PROTECT QLD ISLAND FROM MINING
The Australian Conservation Foundation wants the Federal Government to prove its green credentials by protecting North Stradbroke Island, near Brisbane, from sand mining.
ACF executive director Jim Downey says North Stradbroke is an important test case for the Government.
The call comes after a week-long protest by residents and conservationists, who have blockaded the access road to the sand mine on the island.
